title: Next Goal Wins
tagline: Worst team in the world. Best feed after the match.
about: A burnt-out Dutch coach is sent to American Samoa to turn around the worst football team on the planet.
cue: Serve the mains when the team finally scores a goal.
faces: HAWKERS IN EVERY AISLE. HOLLER AND WAVE.

    Starters31 to 0 taro chipsPaper thin fried taro chips with lime and chilliHow to make it600g taro2 L vegetable oil, for frying1 tsp salt1 lime, zested1/2 tsp chilli flakesPeel the taro and slice paper thin on a mandoline.Fry in the vegetable oil in batches at 175°C until crisp and pale golden.Drain and toss with salt mixed with lime zest and chilli flakes.Samoan oka raw fish in coconutFish cured in lime juice, tossed with coconut cream and cucumberHow to make it400g very fresh white fish fillets4 limes200ml coconut cream1 cucumber2 tomatoes1/2 red onionsalt and pepper, to tasteCut the fish into 1cm cubes and cover with lime juice.Chill until the fish turns white.Dice the cucumber, tomatoes and onion.Drain most of the juice, then stir in the coconut cream and vegetables. Season and serve cold.Palusami coconut spinach parcelsTaro leaves baked in coconut cream, a Samoan feast stapleHow to make itAs written, serves 4Silverbeet leaves wrapped around onion, garlic and seasoned coconut cream, baked in foil parcels until rich and soft, served with roast taro.Heat the oven to 180°C.Peel 800g taro, cut into chunks, toss in oil and salt and roast 45 minutes.Strip the stalks from 1 bunch silverbeet.Mix 400ml coconut cream with 1 finely diced onion, 1 crushed garlic clove and 1 tsp salt.Stack 3 leaves into a cup in your hand, add a few spoons of coconut mix, fold closed and wrap tightly in foil.Make 8 parcels and bake 40 minutes.Open and serve with the taro.Fried breadfruit with coconut creamNicky Salapu's back in goal. Crush the garlic and chop the ginger.Fry the chicken in the vegetable oil with the garlic and ginger until browned, then add the carrots and onion.Add the noodles, soy sauce and water and toss until the noodles soak it all up.Pisupo corned beef with fried riceThe tinned corned beef that turns up at every Samoan tableHow to make itAs written, serves 4Tinned corned beef fried with onion, tomato and cabbage until crispy at the edges, over garlic fried rice with a squeeze of lime and soy.Cook 2 cups rice the day before and chill.Fry 1 sliced onion in oil for 3 minutes, add 2 diced tomatoes and a quarter of a cabbage, shredded, and cook 5 minutes.Break in 340g tinned corned beef and fry over high heat, stirring now and then, until browned in spots.In another pan, fry 3 crushed garlic cloves in oil, add the rice and 2 tbsp soy and toss until hot.Serve the beef over the rice with lime.SweetsPanipopo coconut bunsSoft yeast buns baked in sweet coconut creamHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast50g caster sugar, for the dough50g butter, softened300ml warm water400ml coconut cream100g caster sugar, for the sauceMix the flour, yeast, the 50 g of sugar, butter and warm water into a dough.Prove the dough, which is the resting time.Shape 12 buns into a baking dish.Mix the coconut cream with the 100 g of sugar for the sauce and pour over.Bake at 180°C until golden and sticky.DrinksJaiyah's Samoan hot chocolateDark chocolate melted into hot water and milk, served in mugsHow to make it150g dark chocolate500ml hot water500ml milk3 tbsp caster sugar1 cup ice, if serving coldMelt the chocolate into the hot water.Whisk in the milk and sugar and heat until steaming.Serve hot in mugs, or cool and pour over ice.Fresh green coconutHalftime against Tonga, one goal still needed.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
